archetype.name: Dual-Threat (arm-first)
archetype.definition: A nine-year starter whose legs are still a weapon but now show up mostly as scrambles off dropbacks, while his passing carries an offense that would rather run.

report.headline: Career-best passing efficiency, but an ankle and thin line test it
report.take:
Lamar Jackson's 2026 is the most efficient passing he has put on tape. His 10.74 adjusted net yards per dropback leads all 42 qualifiers, and his 10.07 yards per attempt beats the 8.8 of his 2024 season, which ranked second. His CPOE of 8.29 is nearly double his previous career high of 4.55. The running is still there, with 144 yards that lead all QBs, but its shape has changed. Only 6 of his 19 carries were designed runs. The rest came from 10 scrambles that produced 107 yards and 6 first downs. He is less a designed-run engine than he was from 2019 to 2024, when he averaged 50-plus rushing yards a game, and closer to a pocket passer who leaves when the play breaks down.

The context explains a lot. Baltimore passes 5.1 points less than game situations predict (25th), so he has averaged just 24 attempts a game. Those throws come in favorable spots, which is why the per-play numbers are huge and the totals sit mid-pack: 14th in passing yards. The protection has helped. The offense's hit rate ranks 3rd, and his pressure-to-sack rate of 26.3% is far healthier than the 43.9% of 2025. When he does drop back, he has been accurate at every level: 0.904 EPA on intermediate throws, 0.745 on deep balls, 79.6% completions short. Under center his CPOE is 20 on 20 attempts, a sign of how well the play-action looks are landing.

The numbers hide how small the sample is and where it is fragile. Ninety-six attempts is a month, not a season. The deep work rests on 18 throws, and Zay Flowers' 1.46 EPA per target on 19 targets is a heater, not a baseline. Third down has been ordinary: 34.8% success, though he faced an average of 9.2 yards to go. The red zone has been negative in EPA with a -7 CPOE, rescued by 4 touchdowns on 14 attempts. His one bad game, a 3.3 passing EPA in the home loss to New Orleans as an 8.5-point favorite, was also his highest-volume game (31 attempts).

Where it heads depends on health more than talent. He played only 52% of snaps in Week 4, and ankle news followed the next day. His coach now says he doesn't know the chances for Sunday. Left guard Jovaughn Gwyn (91% of snaps) is on IR until December, Ronnie Stanley is questionable with a toe injury, and backup interior pieces are hurt too. Expect the efficiency to settle toward his 2024 level, which is still top-ten. Volume stays capped by the run-first plan, and the rushing ceiling is lower until the ankle is clean.

strengths.title: Accuracy at every depth
strengths.body: He is completing passes well above expectation on short, intermediate and deep throws alike, with a season CPOE second among qualifiers. Part of it is scheme, with clean, play-action-heavy dropbacks in a run-leaning offense. Part of it is a real improvement from the 1.76 CPOE of 2025. The level will come down, since it is far above anything in his career, but the 2024 baseline of about 4.5 is a reasonable floor for a healthy Jackson.

strengths.title: Explosive yards per dropback
strengths.body: Leading the position in ANY/A means his dropbacks gain more than anyone's after sacks and picks are priced in. The deep ball drives it: 18 throws produce 0.745 EPA despite a 44% completion rate, which is the normal trade for a vertical passer. This is sustainable in kind, since he ranked 2nd and 6th in yards per attempt in 2024 and 2025, though not at 10-plus.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move the chains
strengths.body: His rushing value now comes mostly from breaking the pocket: 10 scrambles for 107 yards, 6 first downs and 0.48 EPA each. That is what pays for a 3.11-second time to throw. The extended plays turn into first downs instead of sacks, and his pressure-to-sack rate is mid-pack rather than near the bottom as in 2023 and 2025. This is the piece most exposed to the ankle.

concerns.title: Ankle plus a thinning line
concerns.body: He is questionable, and his coach was openly unsure Monday. The 52% snap share in Week 4 suggests the injury cost him half a game already. Even if he plays, Gwyn is out until December, Stanley (92% of snaps) is questionable, and depth guard Vorhees and center Pocic are also hurt. A limited Jackson behind a patched interior is the scenario where his sack rate, already 24th, gets worse.

concerns.title: Efficiency well above his history
concerns.body: A CPOE nearly double his career best on 96 attempts will regress. So will Flowers' EPA per target, more than four times Mark Andrews' 0.319 on a similar volume. None of it says the passing is fake, but projecting 10 yards per attempt forward would be a mistake. The bad-throw rate of 14.6% ranks 25th of 32, which hints that some completions have been kinder than the throws.

concerns.title: Third down and red zone lag
concerns.body: His money downs are flat: 0.01 EPA on third down and -0.07 in the red zone, with a -7 CPOE inside the 20. The third-down number is partly a long-yardage problem (9.2 to go on average). Four red-zone TDs on 14 attempts is a scoring rate the underlying accuracy doesn't fully support. The low volume from a -5.1 pass rate over expected also caps his counting stats.

trend.note: Outside the Week 2 loss to New Orleans (3.3 passing EPA), he has posted 10-plus passing EPA every week. Weeks 3 and 4 each came on just 20 attempts. Volume has dropped from 31 attempts to 20, and his rushing fell to 2 carries in a Week 4 he only half-finished.

nextGame.headline: Atlanta takes away the run; the game rests on his arm
nextGame.body:
Atlanta's defense is built to stop exactly what Baltimore prefers. It allows the fewest rushing EPA per play and the fewest explosive runs in the league, and its overall success rate allowed ranks 3rd. Its pass defense is more ordinary (11th in EPA) but stingy on deep throws (8th), and it hits quarterbacks often (7th) without finishing sacks (27th). For Jackson, that points to a game where Baltimore has to throw more than it likes, against a coverage unit that limits his best area, the vertical game. The softer spot: Atlanta has allowed 277.5 yards per game to quarterbacks, 24th.

Availability drives everything. Jackson's ankle is the headline, and a limited version of him loses the scramble outs that make his long time to throw work against a defense that gets home. His line is short Gwyn, may be short Stanley, and is thin behind them. Chris Moore (6 targets) is out, leaving the passing game even more on Andrews, Flowers and Bateman. On Atlanta's side, Za'Darius Smith (39% of snaps) is questionable after a concussion, which would thin the rush. Atlanta's offense is the league's second-worst passing unit, with its QB room in flux, so Baltimore's defense may hand him short fields.

keyMatchups.title: Baltimore's run game vs. top run defense
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta allows -0.307 EPA per rush, best in the league, against a Baltimore ground game that ranks 7th. If early runs stall, the offense's run-first lean bends, and Jackson's attempts climb above his 24-a-game average. That makes it more of a passing day for him than usual, but a harder one.

keyMatchups.title: Pressure vs. a patched interior
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's hit rate ranks 7th, though its sack rate ranks 27th. Its rushers get to the QB but don't finish. A healthy Jackson turns that kind of pressure into scrambles, but on a sore ankle with a backup guard, those hits turn into sacks more often. His 3.11-second time to throw leaves room for the rush to get home.

keyMatchups.title: Atlanta's anemic passing offense
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's offense ranks 31st in pass EPA and runs far more than expected. It can run, with the 2nd-best rushing EPA, and Baltimore's run defense is 26th. That likely means a slow, possession-heavy game: fewer Baltimore drives, but a favorable scoreboard if Jackson's passing holds up.

nextGame.watch: Whether Jackson is active and how freely he leaves the pocket. A Jackson who won't scramble is a different, much more sackable quarterback against this front.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect elite-adjacent rather than record-setting passing. His per-attempt numbers should drift from 10-plus toward the 8.5-9 range he posted in 2024-25 as the CPOE and Flowers' per-target value come back to earth. The run-first plan keeps attempts in the low-to-mid 20s, so passing yards stay around 220-250 a game. Touchdown volume will track the red zone, where his efficiency has been weaker than his scoring.

The rushing is the bigger unknown. Designed runs are already rare, and the scrambles that carry his rushing value depend on a healthy ankle. A cleaner second half could restore something near his 36-yard average. A lingering injury and a thin line point toward 2025, when he ran for 349 yards in 13 games and his sack rate ballooned.
swingFactors: Stanley's health and the interior line rebuild
Whether Baltimore's pass rate stays below expectation

bets.reason: Atlanta allows the fewest rushing EPA and explosive runs in the league. Jackson had only 6 designed runs in four games, and his scramble production depends on an ankle his coach couldn't vouch for Monday.

Both offenses pass less than situations predict: Baltimore 25th, Atlanta 30th. Atlanta's passing offense ranks 31st in EPA and its defense 8th overall, which points to a grind-it-out game with fewer possessions.

bets.lean: BAL -2.5 (only if Jackson is confirmed active)
bets.reason: Baltimore's best unit, a 2nd-ranked passing offense, faces Atlanta's weaker defensive phase, while Atlanta's 31st-ranked passing offense can't easily keep pace. Without a healthy Jackson, a depleted line and a run game facing the league's best run defense erase that edge.

confidence.note: Eight seasons of career context, but only 96 attempts this year, an uncertain ankle and a shifting offensive line.
